It declares RoleEntity with three fields (name, description, permission), which is the role–permission many-to-many join, plus a constructor that copies in a partial object. It uses the project's shared base class CustomBaseEntity in the same way the other entities do. It contains no business logic that bypasses the module's abstractions, and the files do not split into unrelated concerns. One small redundancy: the uniqueness of `name` is declared twice. The class has @Unique(['name']) and the property has @Index({ unique: true }), so the database may get two unique constraints for one rule. Both declarations sit next to each other in the same file, so the rule is not spread across modules. I treat this as minor cleanup rather than a cohesion failure. Import direction (for example, the domain layer depending on typeorm) is out of scope.
